clue.text: Young girl's spoken of primary injury

indicators.note: something spoken of is heard rather than read, so the sound counts, not the spelling

parts.note: a young girl is a miss; said out loud it gives these three letters
primary and chief both mean main or principal

explanation.surface: Someone is talking about a little girl's first ever injury.
explanation.walkthrough: The homophone covers only the girl's title, not the whole phrase; primary is read as main rather than as a school.
explanation.definitionFit: In older and legal usage mischief means harm or damage done to someone, which is an injury.

clue.text: Ring concerning first annulment

indicators.note: saying one item comes first fixes the order in which the two parts are laid down

parts.note: re means concerning, as in a letter heading
to ring bells is to peal them; a peal is a ring

explanation.surface: A wedding ring matters most when a marriage is being annulled.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads 'Ring concerning', but 'first' puts the concerning part before the ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A repeal is the formal cancelling of a law, so it is a kind of annulment that makes something void.

clue.text: Almost quote Tom, say, coming up with plan

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped
in a down clue, coming up means reading from the bottom to the top, so the order flips

parts.note: to quote is to cite, less its last letter
a tom is a male cat; 'say' marks it as an example

explanation.surface: Someone nearly cites a man called Tom while coming up with a scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom looks like a person's name, but here a tom is a male cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A tactic is a planned course of action to reach an aim, so it is a synonym of plan.

clue.text: Tense cabinet maker breaking spectacles on route to the highest level

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective meaning at the highest level

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

indicators.note: something breaking into a pair forces its way between them, so it ends up inside

parts.note: spectacles look like two round lenses, so two Os
the Prime Minister chooses the cabinet
ST is the abbreviation for street, a route

explanation.surface: A nervous carpenter smashes his glasses on the way up a building.
explanation.walkthrough: The cabinet maker is not a carpenter but the Prime Minister, who picks the Cabinet.
explanation.definitionFit: Topmost describes whatever sits at the very top, which is at the highest level of anything.

clue.text: Cooking back in Sunderland instead of Gateshead is boring

indicators.note: instead of means in place of, so one letter swaps out for another

parts.note: grilling is a way of cooking

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter, so only the end is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the town name
read as Gate's head: the first letter of gate

explanation.surface: Cooking in Sunderland beats cooking in neighbouring Gateshead, which is dull.
explanation.walkthrough: Sunderland and Gateshead are neighbouring towns in north-east England; Gateshead splits into 'Gate's head', its first letter G.
explanation.definitionFit: Drilling a hole is boring one, since to bore means to make a hole with a turning tool.

clue.text: With season curtailed, deer trekking northwards scatter

indicators.note: curtailed means cut short, so the tail letter goes

parts.note: spring, one of the seasons, without its last letter

indicators.note: in a down clue travelling north means going up the column, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: the elk is a large deer

explanation.surface: Herds of deer head north and disperse once their season is cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: The spring season loses its G before the reversed deer is added.
explanation.definitionFit: To sprinkle is to scatter small drops or particles lightly over a surface.

clue.text: Essentially admit nothing about rearing falcon

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so only its central letter is kept

parts.note: the middle letter of the five

indicators.note: a rearing animal rises up on its hind legs, so in a down clue the letters go upward

parts.note: nil means nothing
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A falconer confesses to knowing nothing about raising birds of prey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rearing' suggests raising birds, but it only flips the pair after the first letter, which stays on top of the column.
explanation.definitionFit: The merlin is a small species of falcon found across the northern hemisphere.

clue.text: Romantic page ruined by the woman filming boss

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked and broken up, so these letters are rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: A love letter is spoilt by a woman who is filming it for the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: All fifteen letters, including those from 'the woman', are shuffled together.
explanation.definitionFit: The cinematographer is the director of photography, the head of the camera crew on a film shoot.

clue.text: Shoulder muscle twisted in a court

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

parts.note: taken as written
CT is the abbreviation for court

indicators.note: twisted round means turned the other way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: pec is short for pectoral, a chest muscle

explanation.surface: An athlete pulls a shoulder muscle while playing on a court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoulder muscle' looks like one anatomical phrase, but 'Shoulder' is the verb definition standing alone.
explanation.definitionFit: To shoulder a burden or responsibility is to take it on, which means to accept it.

clue.text: What one must do to get product like tissues?

definitions.text: What one must do to get product like tissues?

parts.words: What one must do to get product
parts.note: surface reading: the arithmetic step that gives a product in sums
setter's reading: tissues come in several layers, or plies, so the word splits into many plus layer

explanation.walkthrough: Product is the result of multiplying numbers; the tissues point to the word read as MULTI-PLY, having many layers.
explanation.definitionFit: Multiplying numbers yields their product, and a multi-ply tissue has several layers of paper.

clue.text: Laid back country club once cleared out tourists with different ways of speaking

indicators.note: going back means travelling the other way, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
the European Community, a former club of countries

indicators.note: a place cleared out has its contents removed, leaving only the outer shell

parts.note: just the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A relaxed old country club empties itself of tourists who speak in other accents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laid back' and 'country club' look like set phrases; they split into a reversal and the old European Community.
explanation.definitionFit: Dialects are regional varieties of a language, each a distinct manner of talking.

clue.text: Annoying to be discovered in Ormskirk in guesthouse

indicators.note: something discovered in a text is found lying within its letters

parts.note: runs across the end of the town and the next two words

explanation.surface: Someone finds an annoying stay at a guesthouse in Ormskirk.
explanation.walkthrough: Ormskirk is a Lancashire market town; its last three letters join the following words.
explanation.definitionFit: To irk is to irritate, so irking is a present participle meaning bothering or vexing.

clue.text: Very loud echo absorbed by book has an impact

indicators.note: something absorbed is taken right inside, so it sits within the other part

parts.note: the Acts of the Apostles, a book of the Bible
fortissimo, the musical marking
Echo is E in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A booming echo is soaked up by a book, which makes an impression.
explanation.walkthrough: The book is the biblical Acts of the Apostles, a common crossword source.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that affects a person or thing influences it, which is to make an impact on it.

clue.text: Tempting every second member of gang in Chittenden to come round

indicators.note: to come round is to turn about, so the kept letters run backwards
taking every second item means stepping over one each time, so alternate letters are kept

parts.note: the first, third, fifth letters and so on

explanation.surface: A tempting offer is made to each gang member in a village to switch sides.
explanation.walkthrough: Chittenden is a village name used here purely for its letters; the alternate letters start from the G.
explanation.definitionFit: Enticing and tempting are synonyms, both describing something attractive that lures a person in.

clue.text: Offered soft beds with covers removed

parts.note: tender means soft, as of meat

indicators.note: taking away the covers strips the outside, leaving only the inner letters

parts.note: the word without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A hotel offered soft beds with the bedclothes stripped off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Covers' suggests bedding, but it means the outer letters of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: To tender something, such as a resignation or payment, is to formally offer it.

clue.text: Brother escaping from erupting subregion describing rocks

indicators.note: an eruption throws material about violently, so the remaining letters land in a new order
whatever escapes from a place leaves it, so those letters are taken out

parts.note: taken as written
BR is the abbreviation for brother

explanation.surface: A monk flees from a region where a volcano is erupting, rocks flying.
explanation.walkthrough: The volcanic surface fits the answer neatly: igneous rocks form from cooled lava.
explanation.definitionFit: Igneous is the adjective for rocks formed from solidified molten magma, so it describes a class of rocks.

clue.text: Still locked, editor's holding up a French competition anyone can enter

indicators.note: in a down clue, holding something up means sitting beneath it, which sets the order

parts.note: un is French for a
an open tournament allows all comers
ED is the abbreviation for editor; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: An editor delays a French contest open to all, while its doors are still locked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holding up' seems to mean delaying, but in a down clue it puts the editor at the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: A door or box that remains locked has not been opened, so it is still unopened.

clue.text: Up to this point, the American footballers lacking energy and resistance

indicators.note: lacking something means being without it, so that letter is removed

parts.note: taken as written
E is the physics symbol for energy
US for the United States
the Football Association, English football's governing body
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: So far, the American football team has played without energy or fight.
explanation.walkthrough: The FA is England's Football Association; energy is dropped from THE only, and resistance is added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Thus far is an adverbial phrase meaning until now, which is the same as up to this point.

clue.text: Block up hideout, heading off to provide protein

indicators.note: with its heading taken off a word loses its first letter

parts.note: to glut is to choke or clog by overfilling
a den is a hideout; drop its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone seals up a hiding place, then leaves to supply food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Block up' reads as sealing the hideout, but it is a separate verb for clogging.
explanation.definitionFit: Gluten is the protein found in wheat and other cereals that gives dough its elasticity.

clue.text: Oscar-winner regularly lied introducing leading parts for Marilyn Monroe (originally Norma)

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the first and third letters

indicators.note: the leading parts of words are their opening letters

parts.note: the opening letter of the first name
the opening two letters of the surname

indicators.note: originally means at the origin, so only the first letter counts

parts.note: the opening letter of the name

explanation.surface: An Academy Award winner fibbed about introducing Marilyn Monroe, born Norma Jeane.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Lemmon won two Oscars and starred with Marilyn Monroe, whose birth name was Norma Jeane, in Some Like It Hot.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack Lemmon, the American actor, won Academy Awards for Mister Roberts and Save the Tiger.

clue.text: Musical mother, on her return, welcomed by hotel

indicators.note: a guest welcomed by a host is taken inside, so one part sits within the other

parts.note: Hilton is a well-known hotel chain

indicators.note: returning means going back the way one came, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A mother who loves musicals is greeted by the hotel when she comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Musical mother' reads as one person; 'Musical' is the definition and stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamilton is Lin-Manuel Miranda's hit stage musical about the American founding father Alexander Hamilton.

clue.text: Tiny writer eating bit of iced fruitcake

indicators.note: whatever eats something takes it inside itself

parts.note: the writer refers to themself as me

indicators.note: a bit of a word is a single letter of it, here the opening one

parts.note: just the first letter
a fruitcake is slang for a crazy person, a nut

explanation.surface: A small author nibbles a piece of iced fruitcake.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter refers to himself as 'writer', giving ME; fruitcake is British slang for an eccentric, a nut.
explanation.definitionFit: Minute, pronounced my-NEWT, is an adjective meaning extremely small, a synonym of tiny.

clue.text: Cyril's rewritten words

indicators.note: something rewritten is recast in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the name with its possessive S

explanation.surface: A man called Cyril has had his words redrafted.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of the possessive is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The lyrics of a song are its words, as opposed to its music.

clue.text: Nuts to take out credit for son's million pounds

indicators.note: taking something out removes it to make room for a replacement
one thing given for another is a swap

parts.note: crackers is British slang for mad
CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
S is the abbreviation for son
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: It is crazy to withdraw credit meant for a son's million pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuts' looks like an exclamation; it means crazy, CRACKERS, whose CR swaps for S and M.
explanation.definitionFit: Smackers is informal slang for pounds sterling or dollars, the units of money.

clue.text: Looked after distribution of refunds fellow ignored

indicators.note: distributing things spreads them around, so the letters are redealt in a new order
whatever is ignored is left out of account, so it is removed

parts.note: taken as written
F is the abbreviation for fellow

explanation.surface: Someone managed the paying out of refunds while one man was left out.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the F from the fodder before rearranging the remaining six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To nurse someone is to care for them, especially when ill, so nursed means looked after.

clue.text: Hit back at noble queen and king taking over diplomat's hotel by day

indicators.note: to take over is to seize control in place of another, so one letter replaces a different one

parts.note: a count is a European nobleman
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina
an attaché is a junior embassy diplomat
K is king in chess notation
Hotel is H in the NATO phonetic alphabet
D is the abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: Aristocrats and royals retaliate after a diplomat's hotel is seized in daylight.
explanation.walkthrough: The K replaces the H in ATTACHE; D follows at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To counter-attack is to strike back in response to an assault, so counter-attacked means hit back at.
